scope: Read-only review of the uncommitted durable USBFS grant integration and cooperative finish lifecycle. File identities below were sampled when this report was written, after the review; the working tree may have been formatted or modified concurrently by the root agent. This is not a source-freeze or runtime validation record.
conclusion: No must-fix issue identified within the inspected integration scope.

checks.name: durable_before_handoff
checks.evidence: App::open_physical awaits Store::reserve before returning Handoff; serve_connection then writes JSON, waits for ACK, and sends the FD.

checks.name: helper_known_fd_order
checks.evidence: Handoff fields drop in declaration order: PhysicalGrant before HandoffTracking. Tracking removes the lease from the active handoff set only after the grant FD drops; Finish waits for active handoff completion.

checks.name: original_owner
checks.evidence: Finish uses kernel peer UID/PID and proc starttime/boot ID; request fields cannot supply an owner identity. UUID is not treated as bearer authorization.

checks.name: complete_baseline
checks.evidence: physical_lifecycle capture/verify compares configuration and the complete sorted interface/alternate/driver set, rechecks generation/configuration, and performs two complete observations.

checks.name: replacement_generation
checks.evidence: A changed or missing original generation is handled as gone; administrator reconciliation requires explicit acknowledge_gone. Reconciliation performs no USB/sysfs writes and does not apply the old baseline to a replacement.

checks.name: administrative_boundary
checks.evidence: PhysicalPending and ReconcilePhysical require UID 0 independently of the ordinary allowed UID set; reconciliation additionally refuses an existing original owner process.

checks.name: preparation_cancellation
checks.evidence: Received grant IDs survive cancellation outside the prepare future. Staged source FDs drop before Finish; cancellation during unresolved blocking initialization retains pending records instead of asserting known capability completion.

checks.name: shutdown_order_and_output
checks.evidence: CLI always awaits server shutdown, then close_and_finish before the final stopped event. Finish is not raced against stdout or repeated signals, and all received grant IDs are attempted while preserving the first Finish error.

checks.name: background_task_ownership
checks.evidence: PhysicalBackend::close rejects other registry clones and unresolved resource state, aborts and joins read-only monitors, and joins supervisors before dropping the registry. Monitor blocking observation receives only paths/receipt. Worker supervisors join their internal watchdogs before returning.

checks.name: uncertain_worker_lifetime
checks.evidence: Supervisors tracking Drop detaches instead of aborting physical work on close failure/cancellation/timeout; unresolved state cannot report successful close or trigger Finish.

nonblocking_boundaries: Cooperative Finish is based on the explicitly trusted granted service. This review does not prove that all system-wide duplicated FDs are absent, and the journal does not revoke previously issued capabilities.
Device observations are point-in-time checks and do not exclude an external administrator changing sysfs/device state after observation.
The backend close contract covers its known registry, monitor and supervisor owners. It does not join the vendored nusb global event thread or prove absence of temporary library/internal references.
Persisted journal storage primitives were implemented/reviewed separately. This integration review is not a complete standalone filesystem crash-durability audit.
Software fixtures and static source review do not establish real USB forwarding, device recovery, power-loss durability, real-hardware G1/G2 or general device compatibility.
recommended_regressions: New journal two-guest scenario: normal actual I/O followed by record retirement/reopen; SIGKILL followed by persistent refusal across helper restart; root refusal before physical restoration; root retirement after independently restored state.
Existing physical hot-unplug/reinsert regression, including normal shutdown of gone old generations.
Existing SIGTERM and output-backpressure shutdown regression.
